thesis: Delayed punishment is not proof of safety — those who plot evil remain reachable by Allah in every mode of life, and the spacing before seizure is itself an expression of His ra'fah and rahmah.
notes: Thesis is carried explicitly by Ibn Kathir, who opens the passage with 'Allah informs us about His patience, and how He delays the punishment for the sinners' and closes with '(Indeed your Lord is full of kindness, Most Merciful.) meaning, because He does not hasten to punish' plus the two Sahih hadiths on Allah's forbearance toward the wrongdoer. Every gloss checks out: makr al-sayyi'at as scheming (Qatadah in al-Tabari glosses al-sayyi'at as shirk; al-Jalalayn as the plot against the Prophet at Dar an-Nadwa — the file's broader 'scheming toward corruption' is compatible with both and asserts neither); taqallub as travel/daily going-about (Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj in al-Tabari; Ibn Kathir same); mu'jizin as inability to frustrate Him. The file's one attribution sentence — 'Classical tafsir treats this with shades of gradual diminution, fearful reduction, or taking while fear is already settling around them' — is precisely right and correctly hedged: al-Tabari gives takhawwuf = tanaqqus (gradual reduction, with the Ibn Muqbil shahid and the Azd Shanu'ah dialect note), al-Muyassar gives BOTH ('bi-naqs min al-amwal wa al-anfus wa al-thamarat, aw fi hal khawfihim'), and Ibn Kathir gives the 'seized amid what they most fear' reading via Al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. No countable, superlative or hapax claims anywhere in the file — the 'only/never/always' hits are all rhetorical, not corpus claims. All three inline ayahs match the Uthmani text exactly after normalization. All prose-referenced roots verify against the corpus (qlb/taqallub, khwf/takhawwuf, 'jz/mu'jizin, r'f, rhm). Not ahkam-bearing; no ikhtilaf owed. No quoted tafsir, so no truncation surface. Metadata nit only, not a content issue: frontmatter word_count 1488 vs ~1655 actual body tokens.

thesis: Ibrahim reverses the direction of fear — the real insecurity is not in refusing false gods but in wronging tawhid itself, so true amn belongs only to iman not clothed in zulm.

flags.quote: **And his people argued with him. He said, "Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? ... So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you should know? Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing - those will have security, and they are rightly guided. And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing."**
flags.issue: The quotation mark opened after 'He said,' is never closed until the end of 6:83, so the displayed translation puts 6:82 AND 6:83 inside Ibrahim's own mouth. That makes Ibrahim say 'And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people' — first-person divine speech about Ibrahim in the third person, spoken by Ibrahim. In the standard translation the quote closes after 'if you should know?' (end of 6:81). The error contradicts the file's own body, which correctly reads 6:82 as divine speech ('Then the divine verdict:' and, in the Closing Synthesis, 'Allah answers:'). It also lands on the wrong side of a real recorded ikhtilaf: al-Tabari opens his commentary on 6:82 with 'ikhtalafa ahl al-ta'wil fi alladhi akhbara ta'ala dhikruhu 'anhu annahu qala hadha al-qawl', and the first-listed and preferred view — 'hadha fasl al-qada' min Allah bayna Ibrahim khalilihi wa bayna man hajjahu min qawmihi' — is divine verdict, matching Ibn Kathir ('Allah has testified Ibrahim's statement and affirmed security and guidance'). Identical error is duplicated in the frontmatter `translation:` field, which is what feeds the published page.

notes: Fix is mechanical and must be applied in TWO places — the frontmatter `translation:` value (line 10) and the bolded translation block (line 84): close the quotation after 'if you should know?' and leave 6:82-83 outside the quote. Everything else in the file verified clean. Specifically checked per the task note on the star/moon/sun ikhtilaf (6:76-79): the file does NOT take the dangerous side. Its only reference is passage_context's neutral 'After Ibrahim publicly dissociates himself from every setting object and declares his face turned wholly toward the One who originated the heavens and the earth', and the intro frames the scene as 'His people argue with him after his open declaration of tawhid' — i.e. Ibrahim already a muwahhid making a case, the rhetorical-argument reading, which is exactly Ibn Kathir's frame ('when his people mentioned various doubts and disputed with him about the Tawhid that he called to') and al-Tabari's ('wa qad hadan ... waffaqani rabbi li-ma'rifat wahdaniyyatih'). No prophetic-infallibility exposure; nothing to fix there. Other claims all verify: hajj root = argumentation/contest (corpus root حجج, lemma حاجَّ); 'the argument appears to have included fear: fear of the idols' is exactly al-Tabari ('inna nakhafu an tamassaka alihatuna bi-su' min baras aw khabal') and al-Jalalayn ('haddaduhu bi'l-asnam an tusibahu bi-su''), and the file correctly hedges with 'appears to have'; sultan = proof/warrant per Ibn Kathir from Ibn 'Abbas 'and others among the Salaf'; yalbisu = to clothe/mix (corpus root لبس); 'The hadithically clarified meaning here is shirk as the great zulm' is exactly right — Bukhari and Ahmad via Ibn Mas'ud with the Prophet pointing to 31:13, and al-Tabari's own tarjih ('wa awla al-qawlayn bi'l-sihha fi dhalik ma sahha bihi al-khabar 'an Rasul Allah ... huwa al-shirk'), with al-Jalalayn concurring ('ay shirk kama fussira bi-dhalik fi hadith al-Sahihayn'); the file also correctly guards against the Companions' misreading by writing 'The point is not a faith occasionally accompanied by human weakness in the broad sense'; 'Even the argument belongs to Allah. Hujjah is granted' matches Ibn Kathir ('We directed him to proclaim Our proof against them'). No countable/hapax/superlative corpus claims in the file. thesis: The darkest form of kufr is not merely refusing Allah's blessing but converting that blessing into a system of misguidance that lodges a whole people in ruin while temporary enjoyment disguises the destination.
notes: Thesis is carried directly by the ayah's own two-step (baddalu ... wa-ahallu qawmahum) and by the tafsir. The file's one explicit attribution — 'Classical tafsir often points here to the greatest blessing given to Quraysh: the Messenger, revelation, guidance' — matches al-Tabari verbatim in substance ('kana tabdiluhum ni'mat Allah kufran fi nabiyy Allah Muhammad, an'ama Allah bihi 'ala Quraysh ... fa-kafaru bihi wa kadhdhabuhu') and Ibn Kathir (Ibn 'Abbas: 'in reference to the people of Makkah'; 'Ali: 'the disbelievers of Quraysh on the day of Badr'). Crucially, the file's widening — 'But the phrasing is broad enough to make the pattern wider' — is not an unwarranted extension: Ibn Kathir makes the same move himself ('This includes all disbelievers, for Allah sent Muhammad as a mercy and a blessing to all mankind'), and the file correctly marks it as its own move rather than attributing it. The 'corrupt leaders' framing is likewise grounded, not invented: Qatadah in al-Tabari has 'hum qadat al-mushrikin yawm Badr, ahallu qawmahum dar al-bawar' and al-Dahhak has 'ahallu man ata'ahum min qawmihim'; al-Jalalayn has 'wa-ahallu qawmahum bi-idlalihim iyyahum'. Lexical claims verify: baddalu as substitution/replacement (corpus root بدل, lemma بَدَّلَ); bawar as perishing/ruin — al-Tabari gives the etymology outright ('bara al-shay' yaburu buran: idha halaka wa batala') and al-Jalalayn glosses dar al-bawar as 'al-halak'; ahallu as causing to descend/lodge (al-Jalalayn 'anzalu', corpus root حلل); andad as rivals/counterparts (corpus root ندد); tamatta'u read as exposure not permission is exactly Ibn Kathir ('Allah threatened them and warned them by the words of His Prophet'), reinforced by his citation of 31:24 and 10:70. The structural observation 'Notice the bitter movement: **dar** in the first ayah, **qarar** in the next' is textually verified — دَارَ الْبَوَارِ in 14:28, الْقَرَارُ in 14:29 — and is a plain reading, not a count claim. No countable, hapax, superlative or 'only place' claims anywhere in the file. All three inline ayahs match the Uthmani text exactly after normalization. Not ahkam-bearing, and the file never applies the verse to any named modern group, so no takfir-adjacent adab exposure. No quoted tafsir, so no truncation surface. Metadata nit only, not a content issue: frontmatter word_count 996 vs ~1362 actual body tokens.
